test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The resistance of a metallic wire is R. If the radius of the metallic wire is reduced to half of its initial value while keeping all other parameters the same, the new resistance becomes ______.
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Resistance of a Metallic Wire:**

The resistance of a metallic wire depends on its material, length, and cross-sectional area. The formula for resistance is given by:

**R = ρ × (L/A)**

Where:

 
• R is the resistance of the wire.
 
• ρ (rho) is the resistivity of the material.
 
• L is the length of the wire.
 
• A is the cross-sectional area of the wire.

The cross-sectional area (A) of a wire with circular cross-section can be expressed as:

**A = π × r²**

Where:

 
• r is the radius of the wire.

**Given Data:**

 
• The initial resistance of the wire is R.
 
• The radius of the metallic wire is reduced to half of its initial value, while keeping all other parameters (length and material) the same.

**Analysis:**

Let the initial radius of the wire be r₁ and the initial cross-sectional area be A₁. Then:

A₁ = π × (r₁)²

Now, the resistance of the wire is:

R = ρ × (L / A₁)

When the radius of the wire is reduced to half of its initial value, the new radius becomes:

r₂ = r₁ / 2

The new cross-sectional area (A₂) will be:

A₂ = π × (r₂)²

Substitute r₂ = r₁ / 2 into the equation for A₂:

A₂ = π × (r₁ / 2)²

A₂ = π × (r₁)² / 4

Thus, the new cross-sectional area is one-fourth of the initial cross-sectional area:

A₂ = A₁ / 4

The new resistance of the wire, R₂, is given by:

R₂ = ρ × (L / A₂)

Substitute A₂ = A₁ / 4 into the equation for R₂:

R₂ = ρ × (L / (A₁ / 4))

R₂ = ρ × (L × 4 / A₁)

R₂ = 4 × (ρ × (L / A₁))

R₂ = 4 × R

**Thus, the new resistance becomes 4 times the initial resistance, i.e., 4R**
